why: 40 characters of base64 alphabet with no prefix, no keyword and no assignment — the one shape the inline table records as uncaught, kept here so the corpus states its own gap
a commit hash: 40 characters, hex alphabet, no prefix, no keyword — the benign neighbour that makes entropy alone unusable on the case above
a credential-named variable with a quoted value — the shape a config file most often leaks
the same shape carrying a setting rather than a credential; a rule keyed on the variable name alone would redact this
a package-lock integrity hash is base64 of a digest and looks exactly like a key; GitHub's own scanners produced ~18,000 alerts on five such repositories, all false
the one line in the same file that IS a credential — same file, same quoting, and the prefix is the only thing that separates them
go.sum is a file of base64 digests beside module names; a shape rule with no file awareness flags every line of it
a composer.lock dist reference is a 40-character hex run, the same shape as a commit sha and as several token formats
SOPS ciphertext is a secret that is ALREADY encrypted — redacting it costs nothing and flagging it as a leak is wrong; it is the canonical over-report
a certificate is PUBLIC by definition and shares its envelope with a private key; the word between BEGIN and the dashes is the whole difference
the same envelope as the certificate above, and this one must never leave the machine

text: export API_KEY=<your-api-key-here>   # replace this before running
why: a README placeholder in an assignment shape; a rule keyed on `KEY=` alone reports every quickstart in every repository
a UUID is high-entropy, hyphenated, and identifies nothing secret; entropy rules eat these first
26.7% of one 12,433-record study's findings came from test paths, and excluding them cut a model's false positives by 76% — the path is the signal, not the value
a JWT header and payload are base64 of PUBLIC json; only the third segment is the secret, and this one is elided
the complete token, third segment present — the shape the benign case above is one segment away from
an image digest is a 64-character hex run in a line that also contains a hostname, which is the two signals a connection-string rule looks for
a conflict marker is punctuation a scrubber must leave alone; it has been mistaken for a delimiter before
a data URI is a long base64 run in an assignment; length and alphabet alone cannot tell it from a key, and it appears in generated HTML by the thousand
a webhook URL is a credential with no key-shaped token in it — the PATH is the secret, which a token-shape rule cannot see
